title: Maximize Number of Subsequences in a String
summary: Given a string text and a pattern of length 2, determine the maximum number of times the pattern can appear as a subsequence in text after inserting either of the pattern's characters exactly once.
statement: Given a string text and a pattern of length 2, determine the maximum number of times the pattern can appear as a subsequence in text after inserting either of the pattern's characters exactly once.
constraints: pattern has exactly two lowercase characters, which may be equal.
Insert exactly one occurrence of either pattern character anywhere in text.
Maximize the number of pattern occurrences as length-two subsequences.
hints: Count existing subsequences, then compare the gain from inserting either endpoint character.
A new first character at the front pairs with every existing second; a new second at the end pairs with every existing first.
Scan to count existing ordered pairs and first-character occurrences; add max(first_count,second_count).
Front and end placements maximize the respective insertion’s partners, and insertion does not change any preexisting subsequence.
editorial: Front and end placements maximize the respective insertion’s partners, and insertion does not change any preexisting subsequence.

tests.explanation: The text already has two ac subsequences; inserting a at the front adds two more, totaling four.
Four ab subsequences already exist; the best insertion adds two, giving six.
